extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing MPEP §706.02 guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining prior-art dates under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) for U.S. patents, U.S. application publications, and WIPO publications, including how international applications, benefit/priority claims, and copending applications affect the 102(e) date. Includes flowchart checks, examples, and form paragraphs to be used in Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IA-filed-on-or-after-November-29-2000-entitles-international-filing-date-to-102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application (IA) was filed on or after November 29, 2000; designated the United States; and published under PCT Article 21(2) in English, then the international filing date is a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such an international application properly claims benefit to an earlier-filed U.S. or international application, or to an earlier-filed U.S. provisional application, apply the reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of the earlier filing date, assuming all the conditions of 35 U.S.C. 102(e), 119(e), 120, or 365(c) are met. The subject matter used in the rejection must be disclosed in the earlier-filed application in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, for that subject matter to be entitled to the earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: IA-filed-on-or-after-November-29-2000-but-did-not-designate-US-or-not-published-in-English
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed on or after November 29, 2000, but did not designate the United States or was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2), do not treat the international filing date as a U.S. filing date for prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply the reference as of its international filing date, its 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) completion date, or any earlier filing date to which such an international application claims benefit or priority. The reference may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date, or under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of any later U.S. filing date of an application that properly claimed the benefit of the international application (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: IA-filed-prior-to-November-29-2000-use-pre-AIPA-provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, apply the reference under the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 374 prior to the AIPA amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) For U.S. patents, apply the reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as of the earlier of the date of completion of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1),(2) and (4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit of the international application; (b) For U.S. and WIPO application publications directly resulting from IAs filed prior to Nov. 29, 2000, never apply these references under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — apply as of publication dates under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b); (c) For U.S. application publications of applications that claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 or 365(c) of an IA filed prior to Nov. 29, 2000, apply 102(e) as of the actual filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: do_not_use_foreign_priority_dates_as_102(e)_dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applications’ filing dates that are claimed (via 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), (f), or 365(a) or (b)) in applications which have been published as U.S. or WIPO application publications or patented in the U.S. may not be used as 35 U.S.C. 102(e) dates for prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes international filing dates claimed as foreign priority dates under 35 U.S.C. 365(a) or (b). (In re Hilmer cited elsewhere illustrates no benefit of foreign filing date for 102(e).) Consider foreign priority claims only under appropriate other statutes, not for establishing a 102(e) date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 111(a)_application_with_no_benefit_or_priority_claims_gets_its_own_filing_date_for_102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reference publications and patents of patent applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) with no claim for the benefit of, or priority to, a prior application, the prior art dates under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) accorded to these references are the earliest effective U.S. filing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, a publication and patent of a 35 U.S.C. 111(a) application which does not claim any benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120 or 365(c) would be accorded the application’s actual filing date as its prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). (See Examples 1 and timelines.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 111(a)_application_with_benefit_to_prior_US_app_acquires_earlier_filing_date_for_102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications that claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to a prior U.S. provisional application or under 35 U.S.C. 120 to a prior nonprovisional application, the prior art dates under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) are the earlier filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is true assuming the earlier-filed application has proper support for the subject matter as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120. (See Example 2.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 111(a)_application_claiming_foreign_priority_receives_US_filing_date_for_102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications that claim priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) to a prior foreign-filed application, no benefit of the foreign filing date is given under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, a publication and patent of such a 111(a) application would be accorded its U.S. filing date as its prior art date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). (See Example 3 and In re Hilmer.)

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO_publication_may_have_earlier_102(a)_or_102(b)_date_than_US_documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should be aware that although a publication of, or a U.S. Patent issued from, an international application may not have a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date at all, or may have a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) date that is after the effective filing date of the application being examined, the corresponding WIPO publication of an international application may have an earlier 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check WIPO publication dates and languages separately; even where 102(e) does not apply, the WIPO publication can be prior art under 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: indicators_to_identify_international_applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether a reference is a U.S. patent or U.S. application publication of an International Application (IA) after national stage entry, look for any of the following indicators: “35 U.S.C. § 371,” “§ 371,” “(22) PCT Filed:,” and/or “(86) PCT No.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these indicators as the first step in the flowchart for determining applicable 102(e) dates. Follow subsequent decision nodes regarding IA filing date relative to Nov. 29, 2000 and whether the WIPO publication was in English and designated the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: consider_proper_benefit_claims_under_specific_statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering earlier filing dates for 102(e), consider benefit claims properly made under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to U.S. provisional applications, 35 U.S.C. 120 to U.S. nonprovisional applications, and 35 U.S.C. 365(c) involving international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) when determining 102(e) dates. Ensure the benefit claims are properly made and that earlier applications provide adequate support (see 112, first paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: IA_published_in_non-English_language_after_Nov29_2000_has_no_102(e)_date
rubrics_metrics.description: All references (WIPO publication, U.S. application publication, U.S. patent) of an international application that was filed on or after November 29, 2000 but was not published in English under PCT Article 21(2) have no 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such references may be applied under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates, but never under 35 U.S.C. 102(e). If a later-filed U.S. nonprovisional application claimed the benefit of the IA, the 102(e) date of the patent or publication of the later-filed U.S. application would be the actual filing date of the later-filed U.S. application. (See Example 5.)

rubrics_metrics.name: IA_filed_prior_to_Nov29_2000_patent_has_102(e)_date_of_371_completion
rubrics_metrics.description: For an IA filed prior to November 29, 2000, the U.S. patent issued from that IA has a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date equal to the date of fulfillment of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(1), (2) and (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application publications (WIPO and U.S.) from such an IA do not have any 35 U.S.C. 102(e) prior art date and should be applied, if at all, under 102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates. (See Example 6.)

rubrics_metrics.name: continuation_of_IA_rules_follow_IA_original_filing_and_publication_language
rubrics_metrics.description: When a U.S. 35 U.S.C. 111(a) application is a continuation of an IA, determine the IA’s filing date and whether the IA designated the U.S. and was published in English to decide the 102(e) date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IA was filed on or after Nov. 29, 2000 and published in English and designated the U.S., then the WIPO publication, the U.S. application publication, and the U.S. patent of (or claiming benefit of) that IA have the 102(e) prior art date of the international filing date or earlier effective U.S. filing date. If the IA was not published in English, no 102(e) date is given for the IA publication and the U.S. publication/patent get the actual U.S. filing date of the continuation. (See Examples 7–9 and Additional Benefit Claims sections.)

rubrics_metrics.name: provisional_102(e)_rejection_when_copending_app_has_common_inventor_or_common_assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: If (1) at least one common inventor exists between the applications or the applications are commonly assigned and (2) the effective filing dates are different, then a provisional rejection of the later-filed application under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisional rejection is appropriate where, if the earlier-filed application is published or becomes a patent it would constitute actual prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102. Use form paragraph 7.15.01. The provisional rejection can be overcome in the same manner as a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection (see MPEP §706.02(b)), or by abandoning the applications and filing a new application containing the subject matter of both. The rejection might be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor of this application (i.e., not “by another”), or by an appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131. This rejection may not be overcome by the filing of a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). If claims would have been obvious over the other copending application, use form paragraph 7.21.01. If conflicts exist, also consider provisional double patenting rejections using form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32. If evidence shows 102(f) or (g) issues, make appropriate rejections (7.13/7.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: no_provisional_rejection_when_no_common_inventor_or_assignee_and_unpublished
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee or common inventor and the application was not published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b), the confidential status of applications under 35 U.S.C. 122(a) must be maintained and no rejection can be made relying on the earlier filed, unpublished application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing dates are within 6 months of each other (3 months for simple subject matter) interference may be proper — see MPEP Chapter 2300. If the earliest effective filing application will not be published under 122(b), it must be allowed to issue once statutory requirements are met; after the patent issues/publishes it may then be used as a reference under 102(e) in the still-pending application. (See II. Copending applications having no common inventor or assignee.)

rubrics_metrics.name: subject_matter_must_satisfy_35_U.S.C._112_first_paragraph_for_earlier_date
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter used in a rejection must be disclosed in the earlier-filed application in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, in order for that subject matter to be entitled to the earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying an earlier filing date (e.g., benefit to an earlier U.S. application or IA), verify that the earlier application’s disclosure provides proper written description and enablement for the claimed subject matter to establish entitlement to the earlier date.

rubrics_metrics.name: flowchart_decision_nodes_and_output_actions_for_102(e)_dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided flowcharts (Chart I and Chart II) to determine 35 U.S.C. 102(e) dates: key decision nodes include whether the reference is an IA after national stage entry, whether IA was filed on/after Nov. 29, 2000, whether the IA designated the U.S., and whether the WIPO publication was in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flowchart outputs: (a) For patent and U.S. application publication where IA meets Nov. 29, 2000 + designation + English publication: §102(e) date = international filing date or earlier effective U.S. filing date (Form Para 7.12); (b) If IA does not meet those criteria: no §102(e) date and reference is prior art under §102(a) or (b) as of publication/grant date (Form Para 7.08/7.09); (c) For patents based on IA filed prior to Nov. 29, 2000, §102(e) date is the §371(c)(1),(2) and (4) date (Form Para 7.12.01); (d) For U.S. application publications of certain continuations, §102(e) date may be the actual U.S. filing date of the U.S. application that claimed benefit to the IA (Form Para 7.12). The flowcharts also reiterate: consider benefits properly made under §§119(e),120,365(c); do NOT consider foreign priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: form_paragraphs_to_use_in_102_rejections_and_when_to_cite_them
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the specified form paragraphs in making appropriate rejections: ¶7.07 (Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 102), ¶7.08 (102(a)), ¶7.09 (102(b)), ¶7.10 (102(c)), ¶7.11 (102(d)), ¶7.12 (102(e) per AIPA/IPHTTA), and ¶7.12.01 (pre-AIPA 102(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: the statute quotation (7.07) is required only in first actions on the merits and final rejections; form paragraphs 7.07–7.14 are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action. Identify the particular part of the reference relied upon to support the rejection. Use Form Paragraph 7.15.01 for provisional rejection (common assignee/at least one common inventor).
